note: Side-by-side comparisons of two structures learners confuse, written for this project.
why: The corpus explains each structure on its own page and never sets two against each other, so a comparison cannot be extracted from it. Unlike the paradigm tables in tables.json — which are closed systems anyone can check — choosing WHICH two structures to contrast, and what to say about each, is a teaching decision. That is why each one is attached to a topic that actually teaches at least one side of it, why the distinctions here are the standard ones every reference grammar states, and why this file says out loud that it was written here.

rows.left: Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank bin.
rows.right: Ich bleibe zu Hause, denn ich bin krank.

rows.left: one single event in the past
rows.right: something repeated, or in the present and future

rows.left: Als ich zehn war, zogen wir um.
rows.right: Wenn ich Zeit habe, koche ich.
Does it happen more than once?
second — and trotzdem itself takes first place

rows.left: Obwohl es regnet, gehen wir spazieren.
rows.right: Es regnet. Trotzdem gehen wir spazieren.

rows.left: haben, sein and the modal verbs use the Präteritum in speech too — ich war, ich hatte, ich musste
rows.right: ich bin gewesen and ich habe gehabt exist, but sound heavy
a position, with no change of place

rows.left: Ich hänge das Bild an die Wand.
rows.right: Das Bild hängt an der Wand.
can be left out, or added with von
the doer is unknown, obvious or beside the point

rows.left: reporting what someone said, without judging it
rows.right: marking something as unreal: a wish, a condition, a polite request

rows.left: Er sagt, er habe keine Zeit.
rows.right: Wenn er Zeit hätte, käme er.

rows.left: when the Konjunktiv I form looks exactly like the indicative — sie haben — it says nothing
rows.right: so the Konjunktiv II is used instead: sie hätten
